SHENZHEN, China — South Korea is closely watching how matters affecting the Korean Peninsula may be handled at the U.S.-China-Russia summit, Thursday, according to a Cheong Wa Dae offiical.
“Since we won’t be at the table, we are naturally interested in how issues that concern us will be addressed,” he said. “We believe we need to take appropriate steps on our end, and we are doing so.”
On Thursdsay, the three-way meeting will take place among U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China.
Asked about speculation that the meeting could become a “second Yalta,” the official said many observers doubted it would play out that way, pointing to differences in how the three countries view the 1945 conference.
“China, which is hosting the meeting, may itself see the decisions made at Yalta as having come at its expense,” he said, adding that Beijing’s perspective differs from those of Washington and Moscow.
At Yalta, the leaders of the U.S. the United Kingdom and the Soviet Union met to discuss the final stages of World War II and the postwar order.
